_comment: The project's matched-decompilation registry. Every entry has been proved
byte-identical against the retail DOL by research/tools/matching-decomp/match.py.
Re-prove the whole file with:  python src-match/verify.py
`exact_bytes` false is NOT a weaker result: it means the object carries a
relocation whose operand field is legitimately zero before linking, and the
match was established on the relocation's SYMBOL instead. See zz_00122c8_.
`iterations` is the number of candidate C sources written before the oracle
returned MATCH. It is the number that sizes an LLM loop, and it is measured
from the retail encodings and the link map. "seed" names which seeder wrote it
and how many model calls and permuter steps it took to reach MATCH -- for every
entry so far, zero and zero. "source_sha256" covers the C below the provenance
header of the referenced file, not the header itself. See docs/matching-loop.md.

compiler.fork_note: This project extends the pinned commit. `python research/tools/matching-decomp/mwcc_fork.py --check` says whether the checkout at .tools/mwcc-rs carries the changes; --apply installs them over a fresh extract of the pinned tarball, byte for byte. TOOLCHAIN.md section 5 lists what each change does and what it unlocks. Entries below marked `needs_fork` do NOT match on the unmodified pinned commit.
compiler.build_label_note: GC/2.5, GC/2.6 and GC/2.7 are the SAME code generator in mwcc-rs; they differ only in the object .comment marker, which a linked DOL does not preserve. The label is the spike's prior, not a measured result.
